title: Nintendo Gamecube Small Discs Reason
report:
I think there has been some misconceptions about the Wii U, so let me set it right. Firstly, the new console did use standard DVDs for games and storage media playback — Nintendo switched to full-size discs with the release of WiiU. Although you can still find old, official statements from 2006 that claim a bigger market share of miniDVDs would lead to "a reduction in piracy", they've since been proven false.
 
That not entirely surprising given the small size DVDs used by Nintendo for GameCube games and the early success of modding on the Xbox was largely due to this very reason. Despite Microsoft's use of more standard, widely-adopted DVDs it seems the company didn't repeat such a mistake with its next-gen console.
Let's move onto the Wii U. Although there been no new hardware announcements from Nintendo since, we can speculate what could've been, but won't know for sure. Rumors a Blu-ray drive has surfaced in patents and now a prototype has shown at this year CES, so maybe they'll jump to larger storage next-gen.
Let me know in the comments what would you like see from Nintendo next.

It seems that GameCube miniDVDs were a bit of an experiment, but they had some interesting effects on gaming. The use of proprietary discs meant that pirates couldn't easily copy games, which was good for gamers and developers alike. However, they weren't without their drawbacks — mainly the storage capacity and size. That makes me wonder if we'll see a return to more conventional media in future Nintendo consoles.

I'm curious what are your thoughts on GameCube miniDVDs? Do you think we'll ever see this sort of innovation again?
